thread:
Alex R: heads up — Polaris is seeing sustained TPS > planned headroom on their dedicated pool since 09:04 UTC, clients getting 429s and some 500s.
Maria S: got the report. Any spikes tied to a release or campaign? :thinking_face:
polaris-support: yes, we shipped a marketing blast at 08:50 and traffic ramped quickly. Most errors are 429/Throttle or 502 with long tail latencies.
Jon P: can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and a short log sample? we need to confirm admission control is tripping vs proxy auth failing.
polaris-support: repro curl: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` — returns `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` after ~120ms. log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T09:06:12Z pool=dedicated-polaris tps=1950 headroom=120 burst_credits=0 admission=deny reason=burst_credit_exhausted
2026-03-15T09:06:14Z proxy lat=1.2s backend=runtime timeout=500ms status=502
```
Ashley L: burst_credits=0 is the red flag. Did the autoscaler kick? any prewarm or reserved throughput config?
polaris-support: pool is Dedicated, reserve=1500 tps, burst_buffer=300. Autoscale shows no new nodes for that minute.
SRE Bot: alert: admission_control.evictions > 200 in 5m for pool=dedicated-polaris. Suggest checking admission policy and burstAccounting lag.
Alex R: billing-bot note — Billing Bot, can you confirm whether burst credits were debited properly for their account? Sometimes billing lag causes credits to not appear.
Billing Bot: billing check: account POLARIS-44 had burst credit bucket update delayed due to a write queue stall at 09:05 UTC. Credits applied at 09:08 UTC (3m lag).
Jon P: that explains 3m window of zero credits. But autoscale not triggering is odd — maybe admission controller thresholds prevented scale because of queueing.
Maria S: possible noisy neighbor? any single client sending huge streaming sessions consuming concurrent capacity?
polaris-support: yes one internal client (analytics) opened long-running streaming sessions — 60 concurrent streams, high token churn. We throttled them but after the campaign they kept open sessions.
Ashley L: immediate mitigations:
- ask polaris to close idle streams (we can force-cut short-lived sessions)
- temporarily raise burst_buffer for this pool or seed extra reserved capacity
- kick autoscaler to re-evaluate or force-add a node
Jon P: longer term: add guardrail to treat long-lived streams separately (stream_concurrency limit) so they don't starve burst credits.
Alex R: action items: (1) @polaris-support close analytics streams now (2) I will request a 10m manual prewarm + bump reserved to 1800 (3) @billing-bot investigate write queue fix root cause and if credits were retro-applied (4) SRE to add quickplaybook step to force autoscale when admission_evictions spike.
polaris-support: closing streams now. will confirm when errors drop.
SRE Bot: replicate command to force node add: `redwoodctl scale pool dedicated-polaris --add-nodes 1 --reason \"surge prewarm\"` — requires ENG-SRE approval.
Jon P: if anyone running repro locally, use this quick check to see admission path:
```
# run 200 parallel reqs for 60s
hey -n 10000 -c 200 -h "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# watch admission metrics:
kubectl logs -l app=admission-control -c admission | grep polaris | tail -n 50
```
Ashley L: after streams closed we saw credits start to refill and 429s dropped at ~09:12 UTC. Will follow up with a postmortem on how marketing campaigns can trigger analytic backfills.
Maria S: thanks. please add a short note on updating runbooks with a step to query `burst_credits` and `admission.evictions` in the first 2 minutes of a surge.
Alex R: agreed. tagging ENG-SRE and Billing for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
polaris-support: thanks team — will keep this channel updated with customer notes for the postmortem.
